fr_guerre_noun.hook: Read la guerre on the upper-left plaque; connect the sober memorial term with war. No violent image.
fr_guerre_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_paix_noun.hook: La paix, PEH: the dove and olive branch bring peace to the gallery.
fr_paix_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_armee_noun.hook: L’armée, ahr-MAY, resembles army: the whole orderly model formation represents the institution.
fr_armee_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_bataille_noun.hook: La bataille, bah-TAHY: connect battle with the second upper-left museum plaque.
fr_bataille_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_colonel_noun.hook: Le colonel, koh-loh-NEHL: the gold rank details distinguish the colonel’s dress uniform.
fr_colonel_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_combat_noun.hook: Le combat, kohn-BAH, shares the English spelling; read it on the upper-right plaque.
fr_combat_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_ennemi_noun.hook: L’ennemi, ehn-MEE: enemy is a label used from one side’s perspective. Keep the lower-right plaque neutral.
fr_ennemi_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_militaire_adj.hook: Militaire, mee-lee-TEHR: the uniform fabric is military fabric; the adjective sits in the center.
fr_militaire_adj.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_garde_noun_f.hook: La garde, GAHRD: three ceremonial guards form one body, the Guard. Feminine collective, not le garde, an individual guard.
fr_garde_noun_f.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.
fr_garde_noun_f.note: La garde here means a body of guards, rather than guard duty or an individual guard.
ex: La garde protège l’entrée du palais.
The Guard protects the palace entrance.

fr_solde_noun_f.hook: La solde, SOHLD: coins beside the pay ledger are a soldier’s pay. Feminine; distinguish le solde, an account balance, and les soldes, sales.
fr_solde_noun_f.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.
fr_solde_noun_f.note: La solde is feminine military pay. Le solde is an account balance; les soldes are sales.

fr_lutte_noun.hook: La lutte, LEWT: the upper-left plaque records a struggle. Read the term without depicting violence.
fr_lutte_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_troupe_noun.hook: La troupe, TROOP: the little uniformed group is one troop or unit.
fr_troupe_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_victoire_noun.hook: La victoire, veek-TWAHR: a laurel wreath is the museum’s sober symbol of victory.
fr_victoire_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_soldat_noun.hook: Le soldat, sohl-DAH: the single ordinary uniform represents one soldier, unlike the group la troupe.
fr_soldat_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_obus_noun.hook: L’obus, oh-BEW: read the historical term artillery shell on the right-hand plaque. No munition is drawn.
fr_obus_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_avant_garde_noun.hook: L’avant-garde: avant means in front, so the military vanguard goes before the main force. Here this is the military sense, not an artistic movement.
fr_avant_garde_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.
fr_avant_garde_noun.note: Military sense: the detachment advancing ahead of the main force, rather than the artistic movement.
ex: L’avant-garde avance devant le reste de la troupe.
The vanguard advances ahead of the rest of the troop.

fr_embuscade_noun.hook: L’embuscade, ahn-bews-KAHD: connect with English ambuscade or ambush; the lower-left plaque holds the term only.
fr_embuscade_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_affrontement_noun.hook: L’affrontement, ah-frohn-tuh-MAHN: opposing sides confront each other. Read the upper-right plaque.
fr_affrontement_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_bombardement_noun.hook: Le bombardement resembles bombardment: the tall dark plaque preserves the term without depicting an attack.

fr_boulet_noun.hook: Le boulet, boo-LEH: think of a boule, a round ball; historically a cannonball, not a bullet. Read the low brass plaque.
fr_boulet_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.
ex: Ce panneau décrit un boulet de canon.

fr_mobilisation_noun.hook: La mobilisation resembles mobilization: the sealed call-up notice summons people into military readiness.
fr_mobilisation_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.

fr_incorporation_noun.hook: L’incorporation: entering the corps means entering military service. The register records induction, not company incorporation.
fr_incorporation_noun.why: Integrated from the independently reviewed standalone pack; contextual sense and painted cue.
ex: Le registre indique la date d’incorporation du conscrit.
The register records the conscript’s date of entry into service.

fr_recrutement_noun.hook: Le recrutement resembles recruitment: the archival poster seeks recruits before entry into service.

fr_conscrit_noun.hook: Le conscrit, kohns-KREE: connect conscript with compulsory service; the mannequin holds its call-up paper.
